text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has approved a review report on the Egyptian economic reform programme. Its representative in Cairo says that Egypt's foreign currency reserves up to mid-March have increased to $19.2 billion. The budget deficit shrank to 0.8 percent of GDP, he adds.
- Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Agriculture, Youssef Wali, says the government will not interfere in the local elections, which will be held tomorrow.

- Head of the Egyptian Atomic Energy Authority, Hesham Fouad, says that construction work has started at an Egyptian-Argentine nuclear plant near the city of Inshas, some 50 km (30 miles) northeast of Cairo. The 22-megawatt-capacity will cost 350 million pounds ($103 million) to support peaceful uses of energy, he adds.
- Chairman of the Arab Organisation for Industrialisation, General Salah Halaby, says the organisation is willing to cooperate with Arab states in military industries.
- Trades at the stock market up to the end of this year have been valued at 18 billion pounds, says Minister of state for Economic Affairs Youssef Boutros-Ghali.
- A new Moslem Brotherhood group was revealed and 29 people, including five journalists and a lawyer, arrested yesterday.
- The Tourist Chambers Federation has agreed to contribute to the tourism ministry's tourist attraction budget by seven milloin pounds.
